title: Q3 2026 Budget Summary
text:
CONFIDENTIAL — Finance only
Effective 2026-10-05
Q3 2026 Budget Summary
Overview
Total operating costs in Q3 were 4.2 million EUR, 3 percent below plan. Fuel costs rose by 11 percent, offset by lower warehouse rent after the Lviv lease renegotiation.
Headcount
The company employed 312 people at the end of Q3. Eight positions in dispatch remain open.
Salary costs are within plan.
Outlook
Q4 forecast assumes stable fuel prices. A 250 thousand EUR reserve is kept for the new Warsaw hub. These figures are confidential and shared with the finance team only.

title: Expense Policy
section: Expense Policy
text: Effective 2026-03-01. Owner: Finance.

title: Expense Policy
section: Expense Policy > What can be claimed
text: Business travel, client meals, training approved by the team lead, and home office equipment up to 40 EUR per year (keyboard, mouse, headset).

title: Expense Policy
section: Expense Policy > Limits
text:
| Category | Limit | Approval |
|---|---|---|
| Hotel, per night | 120 EUR | Team lead |
| Meals, per day | 45 EUR | Not needed |
| Training | 600 EUR per year | Team lead and HR |
| Taxi | 30 EUR per trip | Not needed |

title: Expense Policy
section: Expense Policy > How to submit
text:
Upload the receipt to the expense tool within 30 days. Claims without a receipt are rejected.
Reimbursement is paid with the next salary.

title: Expense Policy
section: Expense Policy > Not reimbursed
text: Alcohol, fines, personal entertainment and upgrades to business class.

title: Onboarding guide
section: Onboarding guide
text: Welcome to Northwind Logistics! This guide covers your first two weeks. Read it before your first day.

title: Onboarding guide
section: Onboarding guide > Before your first day
text: Your team lead sends you a welcome e-mail with the start time and the office address. HR asks you to upload a copy of your passport and your tax number through the HR portal.

title: Onboarding guide
section: Onboarding guide > Day 1
text:
- Collect your laptop and access badge at the IT service desk on floor 2.

- Set up the corporate VPN — see the “VPN setup” guide.

- Meet your buddy: an experienced colleague who answers everyday questions during your first month.

title: Onboarding guide
section: Onboarding guide > Week 1
text: Complete the mandatory security training (about 40 minutes) and the warehouse safety briefing if your role includes site visits. Both are assigned automatically in the learning portal.

title: Onboarding guide
section: Onboarding guide > Week 2
text:
Agree on goals for the probation period with your team lead. The probation period lasts three months; remote work becomes available after it ends.

Questions? Write to hr@northwind.example.

title: VPN setup
section: VPN setup
text: All remote connections to company systems go through the corporate VPN.

title: VPN setup
section: VPN setup > Install the client
text:
1. Open the Software Center on your company laptop.

2. Install “Northwind VPN” and restart the laptop.

3. Sign in with your company e-mail and approve the push notification on your phone.

title: VPN setup
section: VPN setup > Servers
text:
Choose the server closest to you. The client picks one automatically if you do not.

| Server | Location | Use for |
|---|---|---|
| vpn-kyiv.northwind.example | Kyiv | Default for Ukraine |
| vpn-warsaw.northwind.example | Warsaw | Travel in the EU |
| vpn-backup.northwind.example | Frankfurt | Only when the others fail |

title: VPN setup
section: VPN setup > Troubleshooting
text: If the client cannot connect, check the internet connection, restart the client and try the backup server. If it still fails, open a ticket at the IT service desk and add a screenshot of the error.

title: Інструкція з безпеки на складі
text:
1. На території складу носіть захисне взуття та світловідбиваючий жилет.
2. Не заходьте в зону роботи навантажувача, коли горить жовтий маячок.
3. Вантажі понад 25 кг піднімають удвох або за допомогою візка.
4. Про травму або небезпечну ситуацію одразу повідомте начальника зміни.
5. Евакуаційні виходи мають бути вільними завжди.

title: Remote Work Policy
section: Remote Work Policy
text: Effective 2026-09-01. Replaces the version of 2026-01-15.

title: Remote Work Policy
section: Remote Work Policy > 1. Purpose
text: This policy explains who may work remotely, how remote days are approved and which security rules apply to company laptops outside the office. It applies to all permanent employees of Northwind Logistics.

title: Remote Work Policy
section: Remote Work Policy > 2. Eligibility
text: Employees who have completed the probation period may work remotely up to three days per week. Warehouse and dispatch roles are not eligible, because their work requires physical presence on site. Team leads may approve exceptions for a limited period.

title: Remote Work Policy
section: Remote Work Policy > 3. Approval
text: Remote days are requested in the HR portal at least one working day in advance. The team lead approves or declines the request within one working day. Recurring remote days are approved once per quarter.

title: Remote Work Policy
section: Remote Work Policy > 4. Equipment
text: The company provides a laptop and a headset. Employees may claim up to 40 EUR per year for a keyboard or a mouse through the expense policy. Personal computers must not be used for company work.

title: Remote Work Policy
section: Remote Work Policy > 5. Information security
text: Company laptops must use full disk encryption and the corporate VPN when connected to any network outside the office. Public Wi-Fi without the VPN is not allowed. Lost or stolen devices are reported to the IT service desk within one hour.

title: Remote Work Policy
section: Remote Work Policy > 6. Working hours
text: Core hours are from 10:00 to 16:00 Kyiv time. Employees must be reachable in the team chat during core hours and attend scheduled meetings with the camera on when requested by the organiser.

title: Remote Work Policy
section: Remote Work Policy > 7. Review
text: The policy is reviewed once a year by HR and the information security officer. Questions about this policy go to hr@northwind.example.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 1 Purpose and scope
text:
This manual describes the standard operating procedures of the Hamburg distribution centre (DC) and, where marked, of the Lviv cross-dock. It applies to all permanent employees, temporary agency staff and subcontractors working in the warehouse, the yard and the loading docks. Office functions are covered by the employee handbook.
Where a local instruction contradicts this manual, the manual prevails, unless the local instruction was issued later as a temporary instruction (TI) by the H&S officer. Temporary instructions are listed in the QMS folder and expire on the date stated in them.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 2 Definitions
text:
Term
Definition
Shift lead
The person in charge of one shift; first escalation point for any deviation.
Goods received note (GRN)
WMS record created when a delivery is booked in. A GRN is final after the shift lead confirms it; later corrections need an inventory adjustment.
Quarantine
Physical area and WMS status in which stock may not be picked. Zones Q1 (ambient) and Q2 (2-8 °C).
Pick face
The lowest, hand-reachable location of a SKU from which orders are picked.
Replenishment
Moving stock from reserve locations to the pick face. Triggered by WMS when the pick face falls below its minimum.
Near miss
An event that could have caused injury or damage but did not. Near misses are reported like incidents (section 11).
Cross-dock
Goods leave the site within 24 h of arrival without being put away.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 4 Receiving > 4.1 Booking a delivery slot
text: Suppliers book a delivery slot in the slot booking portal at least 24 hours in advance. A truck arriving without a slot is unloaded only if a dock is free and the shift lead agrees; otherwise the driver gets the next free slot. Slots are 60 minutes for full trucks and 30 minutes for vans. Arrivals more than 30 minutes late lose their slot.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 4 Receiving > 4.2 Unloading and checking
text:
1.
Check the seal number against the ASN before opening the trailer. A missing or different seal is a security incident: do not unload, call the shift lead.
2.
For chilled and frozen loads, take the temperature with the probe at the rear, middle and front of the trailer and record all three values on the GRN.
3.
Count pallets, then cartons per pallet. Mixed pallets are broken down and counted per SKU.
4.
Scan every pallet label. Pallets without SSCC label get an internal label from the inbound office printer.
5.
Compare the count with the ASN. Deviations within the tolerance in 4.3 are accepted and noted; larger deviations are put on hold.
6.
Book the GRN in the WMS. The shift lead confirms the GRN within the same shift.
Damaged goods are photographed on the trailer before unloading1. The driver signs the damage note; if the driver refuses, write “driver refused to sign” and add the time.
1 Photos are uploaded to the WMS GRN record, not to personal phones or messengers.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 4 Receiving > 4.3 Receiving tolerances
text: The table lists the count tolerance and the accepted temperature range per product group. Tolerance 0 means that every deviation is put on hold. Temperature limits apply to the probe value, not to the reefer display.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 4 Receiving > 4.3.1 Probe procedure
text:
Use the calibrated probe from the inbound office (calibration sticker must be valid). Insert the probe between two cartons, not into a carton, and wait 30 seconds. For frozen goods use the drill probe on one sacrificial carton per load; the carton is written off on the GRN with reason code 14. If the three values differ by more than 3 °C, measure two more cartons and record the highest value.
A probe that shows an implausible value (for example +20 °C in a running reefer) is taken out of use and replaced. Report the probe number to QA so that earlier measurements can be reviewed.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 5 Storage > 5.1 Location types
text:
The Hamburg DC has 18,400 pallet locations in 42
aisles: ground-level pick faces, narrow-aisle racking up
to 11 m and a block-stack area for beverages. Each
location has a check digit printed on the beam label.
Put-away is confirmed by scanning the location, never
by typing it.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 5 Storage > 5.2 Put-away rules
text:
The WMS proposes a location. The driver may choose
another free location of the same type only if the proposed one is blocked, and must report the reason. Heavy pallets (over 800 kg) go to levels 0 and 1 only. Hazardous goods go to zone H regardless of the WMS proposal.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 5 Storage > 5.3 Rotation
text:
Food and pharma rotate FEFO, all other goods FIFO. A
pallet with a best-before date shorter than the customer's minimum remaining shelf life is moved to zone S and offered to the clearance channel.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 5 Storage > 5.4 Housekeeping
text:
Aisles are kept clear at all times. Empty pallets are
stacked at the end of the aisle, max. 15 high. Stretch
film and cardboard go to the baler, not to the general
waste. Spills are reported immediately and cordoned
off.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 5 Storage > 5.5 Temperature zones
text:
Ambient +5 to +25 °C, chilled +2 to +6 °C, frozen -25
to -18 °C. Data loggers record every 10 minutes;
alarms go to the shift lead mobile.
NOTE
Rack damage of any kind (bent upright, missing beam lock, impact mark) is reported the same shift. A damaged bay is emptied and blocked in the WMS until the rack inspector releases it. Never straighten a rack upright yourself.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 6 Picking and packing
text: Orders are released to picking in waves. Store orders are released at 22:00 for next-morning delivery; parcel orders are released every hour until the carrier cut-off (see 7.4). Pickers follow the route shown on the RF scanner and confirm each pick by scanning the location and the product.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 6 Picking and packing > 6.1 Short picks
text: If the pick face is empty, the picker reports a short pick on the scanner. The WMS creates an urgent replenishment task. The picker continues with the next line and the short line is picked later by the same or another picker1.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 6 Picking and packing > 6.2 Packing
text:
•
Use the carton size proposed by the packing station. Void fill is mandatory for glass.
•
Pharma orders are packed only at station P1 and P2, with a second person checking batch numbers.
•
Weigh every parcel. A deviation of more than 5 % from the system weight is checked again.
•
Label on the top side, never over a carton edge or tape.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 6 Picking and packing > 6.3 Productivity
text:
The target is 120 order lines per hour for store picking and 60 lines per hour for parcel picking. Productivity figures are used for shift planning and may not be used alone for disciplinary decisions2.
1 Since Rev 6 short picks are no longer written on the paper pick list.
2 Agreed with the works council, see agreement BV-2013-02.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 7 Dispatch > 7.1 Load planning
text: The transport desk publishes the load plan by 18:00 for the night shift. Heavy pallets go at the front of the trailer, the last store to be delivered is loaded first.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 7 Dispatch > 7.2 Dock safety
text: No loading without an engaged dock lock or wheel chocks. The driver hands the key to the loader and gets it back after the seal is applied.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 7 Dispatch > 7.3 Seals and documents
text: The loader enters the seal number in the WMS and on the CMR. Two copies of the CMR stay at the site; one copy goes with the driver.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 7 Dispatch > 7.5 Late trucks
text: A truck that is more than 60 minutes late for its loading slot is reported to the transport desk. The transport desk decides whether the load is reallocated to another carrier. Pallets already loaded stay on the trailer only if the seal can be applied before the driver's legal driving time runs out.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 7 Dispatch > 7.6 Returnable crates
text:
Every store delivery takes back empty crates. The loader counts crates per store and enters the number on the crate ledger; the store manager signs. Missing crates are charged to the store at 3.50 EUR per crate.
SEE MEMO
QMS-2017-04

section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 8 Health and safety
text:
W A R N I N G
Pedestrians and forklifts share the aisles. Walk only on the green walkways. Make eye contact with the driver before you cross a driving lane. Never walk under a raised load.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 8 Health and safety > 8.2 Forklift operations
text:
Only employees with a valid MHE licence for the specific truck type may drive. The driver checks the truck at the start of every shift using the checklist on the truck; a truck that fails the check is tagged OUT OF SERVICE and reported to the shift lead. Speed limit inside the building is 6 km/h, 10 km/h in the yard.
Mobile phones may not be used while driving. Passengers are not allowed. Forks are lowered and the parking brake is set whenever the driver leaves the truck.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 8 Health and safety > 8.3 Battery charging
text: Batteries are charged only in the charging room. Smoking and open flames are prohibited within 10 m. Topping up with distilled water is done by trained staff only, with face shield and gloves. The eye wash station is next to the door of the charging room.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 8 Health and safety > 8.4 Manual handling
text: The recommended maximum for repeated lifting is 25 kg for men and 15 kg for women; heavier items are lifted by two persons or with a lifting aid. Items over 25 kg are marked with a yellow label in the WMS.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 9 Returns and damaged goods
text:
Returns from stores arrive on the own fleet in returnable crates. Every return needs a return authorisation (RA) number from the customer service team. Returns without RA are held in zone X for 5 working days and then scrapped after approval by the site manager.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 9 Returns and damaged goods > 9.1 Product recalls
text:
Recalls are coordinated by QA. On receipt of a recall notice, QA blocks the affected batches in the WMS within one hour; the shift lead moves all stock of these batches to quarantine and confirms the quantity to QA.
Recalled goods are never scrapped on site without written approval of the supplier.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 10 Inventory counts
text:
Since Rev 6 the annual stocktake is replaced by continuous cycle counts. Every location is counted at least once a year; A-items at least four times a year. Counts are blind: the counter does not see the expected quantity.

Adjustments above 500 EUR per line need approval by the site manager. Inventory accuracy is reported monthly; the target is 99.5 % at location level.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 10 Inventory counts > 10.1 Count procedure
text:
1.
The WMS generates count tasks every night; counters receive them on the RF scanner.
2.
Scan the location, count all units, enter the quantity. Do not open sealed cartons; count cartons and multiply by the pack size printed on the label.
3.
If the location holds a SKU other than expected, enter it as a found item.
4.
Recounts are done by a different person, at the latest on the next shift.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 10 Inventory counts > 10.2 Year-end
text:
For the statutory year-end the auditors may request additional sample counts. The site manager plans these with the finance department; picking may be stopped in the affected aisles for up to two hours.
WOM-001 Rev 6 | Effective 01.03.2016

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 11 Incident reporting
text:
Every injury, near miss, fire alarm, spill or security event is reported. The flow below applies to all shifts.
Event happens
Make area safe, first aid
Inform shift lead (ext. 214/215/216)
Shift lead enters report in WMS within 1 h
H&S officer investigates within 3 days
Actions tracked in monthly H&S meeting
Serious injury:
call 112 first,
then the shift lead
Reports are not used to blame individuals. The aim is to find the cause and prevent repetition.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > 11 Incident reporting > 11.1 Fire alarm
text: Leave the building by the nearest exit, do not use the freezer doors as exits. Assembly point is car park P2. Shift leads take the attendance list from the gate and report to the fire warden.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > Annex C Lviv cross-dock (UA) > C.1 Приймання
text: Вантаж приймає зміна, що чергує на рампі L-D1. Перевірте пломбу, кількість палет і температуру для охолоджених вантажів. Товар без ТТН не приймається; повідомте керівника зміни.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > Annex C Lviv cross-dock (UA) > C.2 Час відвантаження
text: Нова Пошта забирає посилки до 17:00 у будні та до 13:00 у суботу. Палети, що не ввійшли в рейс, лишаються в зоні L-X до наступного дня.

title: Warehouse Operations Manual
section: Warehouse Operations Manual > Annex C Lviv cross-dock (UA) > C.3 Охорона праці
text: Ходіть лише зеленими доріжками. Без жилета та захисного взуття на склад не заходити. Про кожен інцидент чи майже-інцидент повідомляйте керівника зміни впродовж години.
